messages:
maria: Heads up — I'm prototyping a new fleet view in Grafana to surface short GPU bursts and thermal drift across racks. Thinking: compact sparklines for each host, a 2D heatmap for short-term burst density, and a single 'burstiness' score per rack. Draft link: https://grafana.internal/d/xyz/fleet-burst-view :eyes:

ash: Love the idea. Two asks: (1) add normalization per-tenant (so big tenants don't drown small ones), (2) please use a recording rule for the burst metric so panels stay snappy.

maria: Yep on normalization — plan is to divide by tenant_assigned_gpus where available. For burst metric thinking 5m increase of active_gpu_seconds / capacity. Example PromQL I used in the prototype:```promql
sum by (rack) (increase(gpu_core_active_seconds_total[5m])) / sum by (rack) (max(gpu_assigned_capacity, 1)) * 100
```

chris: That looks reasonable. Suggest we also compute a z-score over a rolling 24h baseline so we can highlight anomalous bursts vs normal daily peaks. A recording rule would be:```yaml
record: rack:gpu_burst_rate:5m
expr: sum by (rack) (increase(gpu_core_active_seconds_total[5m])) / sum by (rack) (max(gpu_assigned_capacity, 1)) * 100
```

vikram: For the heatmap, can we make the y-axis temperature bands (e.g., <60C, 60-75C, 75-85C, >85C) and color by percent of samples in each band over the window? That helps correlate power throttles with thermal bins.

ash: Also add an annotation stream for infra deploys and power maintenance windows. Those often align with spikes and we should avoid false positives.

maria: Good call. I'll add grafana annotations hooking into our deploy feed and the power-schedule calendar. Planning to include a compact table with the top-3 offending processes/containers per rack too (via logs->metrics join).

chris: Alert tuning idea: we should avoid firing on short, healthy bursts. Proposal: alert when rack:gpu_burst_rate > 30 for 10m AND zscore(rack:gpu_burst_rate[24h]) > 2. That should target abnormal sustained bursts.

ash: And add a secondary cost-oriented alert: sustained rack-level duty_cycle > 50% for >6h -> paging the capacity-planning list. That drives reserved capacity conversations.

maria: Quick note on queries — use `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(gpu_memory_usage_bytes_bucket[5m])) by (le, rack))` for P95 memory pressure per rack. Avoid per-host noisy raw samples.

grafana-bot: Dashboard "Fleet Burst & Thermal Density" updated by maria (link: https://grafana.internal/d/xyz/fleet-burst-view?orgId=1). Version: v0.2.

ash: I'll review the panel layout tomorrow. One UX ask: show an inline sparklines row and then the heatmap, not the other way around — quick glance should show burst history first.

maria: Will reorder. I'll also add a small legend explaining the burstiness formula and the z-score baseline. Planning to submit a Grafana folder PR and a Prometheus rules PR (recording + alerts) by EOD Friday.

chris: Sounds good. @maria can you put the Prometheus rule snippets in the PR description so SRE can sanity-check thresholds?

maria: Yep. I'll include the example YAML and the rationale. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

vikram: One last thought — add a tiny panel showing the cheapest region that could absorb the burst load (based on recent spare capacity) so infra can suggest migration or on-demand shifts. Might help the cost conversation.

maria: Nice: will surface a computed "suggested offload region" field using our capacity API. Ok I'll start iterating and post updates here.

chris: lgtm. Canary the alert to 1 rack for 48h before wide rollout.

maria: Will do the canary and share the results in this thread.

grafana-bot: Annotation added: deploy:maria/branch-burst-view @ 1853001500

maria: Update — deck + PR opened: https://git.internal/infrastructure/grafana-dashboards/pulls/89. Comments welcome.

ash: reviewing now.
